experiment.hypothesis: A compact transformer with convolutional tokenization (4x4 patches, 49 tokens) will outperform linear-embedding ViTs on 28x28 histopathology because the conv stem captures local nuclear morphology and texture patterns that are critical for distinguishing visually confusable tissue classes (background/debris/mucus, smooth muscle/stroma, normal mucosa/adenocarcinoma). The 49-token sequence length provides sufficient spatial resolution for attention to model inter-cellular relationships while remaining short enough to avoid overfitting on ~90k samples. Hidden width 128 with depth 4 balances capacity against the limited spatial information in 28x28 inputs.

decision.rationale: Starting with compact_transformer as the top-priority architecture for 28x28 RGB histopathology. The built-in convolutional tokenizer with 4x4 patches (49 tokens) preserves nuclear-level texture critical for distinguishing confusable classes (background/debris/mucus, smooth muscle/stroma). Hidden width 128 with depth 4 provides sufficient capacity for ~90k samples without overfitting risk. AdamW with cosine decay at lr=2e-4 is well-suited for transformer training. Mild class weighting (1.63:1 imbalance) and label smoothing (0.1) address the documented label ambiguity without destabilizing majority classes. Batch size 256 balances throughput and gradient noise. 30 epochs with early stopping (patience 5) allows convergence while preventing overfitting on the small 28x28 inputs.
